reasons: Status is correct: Section 9 grants only cause- and event-based exits (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/law/IP), so a three-year term (8.1) with no Customer convenience right sits in the rule's walk-away zone — properly classified as missing behaviour rather than an acceptable fallback.

The inserted language tracks the model clause and reaches the preferred position (30 days' notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, no penalty) and also forecloses a Vendor mid-term convenience right, as the redline guidance directs.

The conforming edit to Section 2.1 is necessary, not scope creep: the original 'without reduction or termination rights' would otherwise negate the new right, and the edit preserves the take-or-pay commitment itself (no double-flagging of the volume commitment).
Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change and the three-year no-exit rationale, and offers the longer-notice fallback.

Minor, non-fatal: the inserted paragraph is unnumbered while amended Section 2.1 cross-refers to 'Section 9.4' — worth labelling the new clause 9.4 (the original numbering skips 9.4) to avoid a dangling reference.
